claim: Across skulls, cranial breadth and cranial height are positively associated after accounting for cranial length: the partial correlation coefficient between breadth and height, given length, is at least 0.2.

data_keys.meaning: maximum cranial breadth of each skull, in mm
cranial height of each skull, in mm
maximum cranial length of each skull, in mm

claim: At a given height, the mean forced vital capacity of smokers and of non-smokers differs by at least 0.2 L: the difference between the two group means, after accounting for height, is at least 0.2 L in absolute value.

data_keys.meaning: forced vital capacity of each subject, in litres
standing height of each subject, in cm
True if the subject is a current smoker

claim: Across children, BMI at baseline and the subsequent change in BMI are negatively correlated: the correlation between the BMI level at baseline and the change in BMI by follow-up is at most -0.25.

data_keys.meaning: BMI of each child at the baseline visit, in kg/m2
a second BMI measurement of each child at the baseline visit, in kg/m2
BMI of each child at the follow-up visit five years after baseline, in kg/m2

claim: Across patients, oxygen delivery and oxygen consumption are positively correlated: the Pearson correlation coefficient between them is at least 0.4.

data_keys.meaning: cardiac output of each patient, in L/min
oxygen content of arterial blood of each patient, in mL O2 per dL
oxygen content of mixed venous blood of each patient, in mL O2 per dL
oxygen consumption of each patient measured from expired-gas analysis, in mL/min

claim: In at least 60% of the species, femur length and humerus length are positively associated after accounting for body length: within the species, the partial correlation between femur length and humerus length, given body length, is at least 0.2.

data_keys.meaning: femur length of each individual sampled in each species, in mm
humerus length of each individual sampled in each species, in mm
head-and-body length of each individual sampled in each species, in mm

claim: Across countries, annual lung-cancer deaths and annual cigarette sales are associated after accounting for population: the standardised slope of deaths on cigarette sales, with population accounted for, is at least 0.2 in absolute value.

data_keys.meaning: total lung-cancer deaths in each country in one year, in thousands
total cigarettes sold in each country in the same year, in millions
population of each country, in millions

claim: Across children, BMI at age 5 and the yearly rate of change in BMI between ages 5 and 10 are negatively correlated: the correlation between the two is at most -0.25.

data_keys.meaning: BMI of each child at the annual visits at ages 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 (visits in age order), in kg/m2

claim: Within patients, oxygen consumption rises with oxygen delivery: the mean over patients of the within-patient slope of oxygen consumption on oxygen delivery is at least 0.1 mL/min per mL/min.

data_keys.meaning: cardiac output of each patient at each measurement occasion, in L/min
oxygen content of arterial blood of each patient at each occasion, in mL O2 per dL
oxygen content of mixed venous blood of each patient at each occasion, in mL O2 per dL
oxygen consumption of each patient at each occasion measured from expired-gas analysis, in mL/min

claim: After accounting for body mass, kidney weight and heart weight are positively related: the standardised slope of kidney weight on heart weight is at least 0.25.

data_keys.meaning: combined kidney weight of each rat, in g
heart weight of each rat, in g
body mass of each rat, in g

claim: Age explains at least 10% of the variance in liver mass beyond what body mass explains: the increase in R-squared when age is added to a regression of liver mass on body mass is at least 0.10.

data_keys.meaning: liver mass of each rat, in g
age of each rat, in days
body mass of each rat, in g

claim: Heart weight accounts for at least 10% of the variance in liver weight beyond what body mass accounts for: the increase in R-squared when heart weight is added to a regression of liver weight on body mass is at least 0.10.

data_keys.meaning: liver weight of each mouse, in g
heart weight of each mouse, in g
body mass of each mouse, in g

claim: Across cities, annual offences recorded and the median age of residents are associated after accounting for population: the partial correlation coefficient between offences and median age, given population, is at least 0.25 in absolute value.

data_keys.meaning: total offences recorded in each city in one year
median age of the residents of each city, in years
population of each city, in thousands

claim: The expected change in BMI between baseline and follow-up is smaller for children with a higher baseline BMI: each additional 1 kg/m2 of baseline BMI goes with a change in BMI that is at least 0.2 kg/m2 smaller (slope of at most -0.2).

data_keys.meaning: BMI of each child at the baseline visit, in kg/m2
BMI of each child at the follow-up visit five years after baseline, in kg/m2
BMI of each child of a test-retest sample at two sessions a few days apart, in kg/m2

claim: Baseline BMI explains at least 10% of the variance in the change in BMI between baseline and follow-up (R-squared of at least 0.10).

data_keys.meaning: BMI of each child at the baseline visit, in kg/m2
a second BMI measurement of each child at the baseline visit, in kg/m2
BMI of each child at the follow-up visit five years after baseline, in kg/m2

claim: Across patients, cardiac output explains at least 25% of the variance in systemic vascular resistance (R-squared of at least 0.25).

data_keys.meaning: mean arterial pressure of each patient, in mmHg
central venous pressure of each patient, in mmHg
cardiac output of each patient measured by thermodilution, in L/min
cardiac output of each patient measured by the Fick method from expired-gas oxygen uptake, in L/min
